label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's your post. Swap `@Kavya` for her actual handle when you paste it in.

---

Some of you have seen a post about founders in your own cohort DMing your team with 40% hikes. A lot of you have tagged me. I'm not going to argue with her in public — Kavya (@Kavya) posted it, she's my friend, and a lot of what she said about me just isn't accurate. But I'd rather correct the record than let wrong numbers travel for six months.

First, my mistake, and I want to own it clearly. I knew where both of these engineers were working from day one. I should have called you before making the offers, not after. That was bad form and I'm sorry.

Now the facts:

We put a backend dev opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone. The first person applied on his own on 19 September. The second came in as his referral two weeks later. Nobody from my side DMed anybody. Not one message.

The offer was 22% over their current CTC. Not 40%. Both joined on 3 November.

On ESOPs — we do have a pool. It's small, but it's real, and it's been on paper since January. I should have shown you the paperwork instead of letting you assume it didn't exist.

After the second offer got accepted I WhatsApped you. It sat on blue tick. Then the post came. I'm not going to relitigate that here — I'd rather talk.

And one thing I want everyone to read: the person I work with most in this batch is not the person I have a problem with. Kavya, you sat with me till 1am in the Koramangala office fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I have never forgotten that and I'm not going to let a hiring thread change it.

What I actually want to talk about is the structural problem. We're both Foundry91 cohort 4, demo day was March 2026 — her SitterNest, my DabbaDost, eleven startups in the batch, all hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will keep happening.

So here's the rule I'd like us to adopt as a cohort:

If you are interviewing someone who currently works at another company in the batch, give that founder a heads up before you make the offer. One call. It takes 60 seconds and costs nothing.

I'm not going to reply to comments on her post. This isn't a fight — I'd rather just talk. And if anyone wants to see the job post, the offer letters or the ESOP paperwork, just ask — I'll share.

Kavya — coffee? Or a call? I'm free this week, whenever suits you. Genuinely.

---

**Numbers:** ~447 words, ~2,320 characters. Both inside your limits.

**A few notes on how it's built:**
- The apology comes *before* the corrections, deliberately. That's what keeps it from reading as a fight, and it's what she'll actually feel when she reads it.
- No names of the two engineers anywhere. Only "the first person" and "the second."
- The 22% correction is stated flatly as a fact, not as a complaint — "The offer was 22% over their current CTC. Not 40%." Two short sentences. It reads like a correction, not a counter-attack.
- The blue tick paragraph is included but drops the grievance immediately after ("I'd rather talk"). If you'd rather not put it out there at all, that paragraph can be cut — you'd land at ~418 words.
- I left out the "40% is wrong, not 22% over their CTC" framing of her post since I don't know her exact wording. You may want to check whether she said "up to 40%" or "40% hikes" and adjust that one line to match.
- The coffee/call offer is the last line, phrased low-pressure ("whenever suits you"), which gives her an easy way to say yes without it looking like a public reconciliation performance.

One thing worth doing before you post: if you still have the WhatsApp thread or the offer letters, don't screenshot-and-post, but do send her the offer letters directly. Giving her the 22% figure privately, first, will land very differently than a public correction — and it makes the public post look like transparency rather than escalation.
